title: NOONAN SYNDROME-LIKE DISORDER WITH LOOSE ANAGEN HAIR 1

relationships.phenotype: NOONAN SYNDROME-LIKE DISORDER WITH LOOSE ANAGEN HAIR 1

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 (NSLH1) is caused by mutation in the SHOC2 gene (602775) on chromosome 10q25.2.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 (NSLH1) is caused by mutation in the SHOC2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We discovered that a SHOC2 mutation promoting N-myristoylation of its protein product causes Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.
checks.explanation: The paper directly states this.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 gene is located on chromosome 10q25.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Resequencing of coding exons for the best candidate, SHOC2,
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature and is not stated in the paper; the gene itself is the one the paper studies.

paragraphs.text: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 is a RASopathy (Gripp et al., 2013). It shares features with Noonan syndrome, including characteristic facial features, short stature, and congenital heart defects, particularly dysplasia of the mitral valve and septal defects (Mazzanti et al., 2003; Cordeddu et al., 2009). Its distinguishing features are hair abnormalities: the hair is easily pluckable, sparse, thin, and slow-growing (loose anagen hair) (Cordeddu et al., 2009). Other features include growth hormone deficiency, darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis, hypernasal voice, and cognitive deficits, often with hyperactive behavior (Mazzanti et al., 2003; Cordeddu et al., 2009).

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 is a RASopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Noonan syndrome is a heterogenous rasopathy typically presenting with short stature, characteristic facial features, cardiac abnormalities including pulmonic valve stenosis, ASD and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM)
checks.explanation: The paper calls Noonan syndrome a rasopathy and says the SHOC2 p.Ser2Gly mutation 'causes Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair.' It also places SHOC2 within the Ras-MAPK pathway and discusses the condition alongside other rasopathies. So the disorder being a RASopathy follows directly from the text, even though the paper never says it in one sentence.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 shares characteristic facial features with Noonan syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: While their facial features seemed typical for NS (Fig. 1a)
checks.explanation: Facial features are described as typical of Noonan syndrome.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 shares short stature with Noonan syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We present three children with short stature, the same facial phenotype, macrocephaly
checks.explanation: Short stature is reported in a condition named as Noonan-like.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 shares congenital heart defects with Noonan syndrome, particularly mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects.
checks.evidence_quote: Cardiac anomalies were observed in the majority of the cases, with dysplasia of the mitral valve and septal defects significantly overrepresented compared with the general NS population.
checks.explanation: Cardiac defects are reported, with mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects prominent.

checks.claim: The distinguishing features of Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 are hair abnormalities, with easily pluckable, sparse, thin, slow-growing hair (loose anagen hair).
checks.evidence_quote: A unique feature of the SHOC2 mutation is its association with loose anagen hair.
checks.explanation: Elsewhere the paper describes the hair as easily pluckable, sparse, thin and slow-growing.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 features include growth hormone deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: severe GH deficiency
checks.explanation: GH (growth hormone) deficiency is explicitly reported.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 features include darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Most of them also exhibited darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 features include hypernasal voice.
checks.evidence_quote: The voice was characteristically hypernasal.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 features include cognitive deficits, often with hyperactive behavior.
checks.evidence_quote: mild psychomotor delay with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
checks.explanation: The abstract reports psychomotor delay together with ADHD.

paragraphs.text: Mazzanti et al. (2003) described 3 children with short stature, a shared facial phenotype, and loose anagen hair. They proposed that the condition was a distinct, previously unreported entity, which they called 'Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.' The children's appearance was not completely typical of Noonan syndrome. The authors also noted severe growth hormone deficiency.

checks.claim: Mazzanti et al. (2003) described 3 children with short stature, a shared facial phenotype, and loose anagen hair.
checks.evidence_quote: We present three children with short stature, the same facial phenotype
checks.explanation: Three children with short stature and the same facial phenotype are described, and their hair is described as loose anagen hair.

checks.claim: Mazzanti et al. (2003) proposed that the condition in the 3 children was a distinct, previously unreported entity, which they called 'Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.'
checks.evidence_quote: We postulate that these children may represent a distinct, previously unreported syndrome that we would name "Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair".
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The appearance of the 3 children described by Mazzanti et al. (2003) was not completely typical of Noonan syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Their appearance, not completely typical of Noonan syndrome
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Mazzanti et al. (2003) noted severe growth hormone deficiency in the children with Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.
checks.evidence_quote: severe GH deficiency
checks.explanation: Severe GH (growth hormone) deficiency is reported.

paragraphs.text: Cordeddu et al. (2009) delineated the clinical phenotype of patients carrying the same SHOC2 mutation. The patients had a distinctive combination of Noonan-like features and loose anagen hair. They also had short stature, frequently associated with proven growth hormone deficiency; darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis; and a characteristically hypernasal voice. Cardiac anomalies were present in most cases, and mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects were significantly overrepresented compared with the general Noonan syndrome population. The patients also had cognitive deficits and distinctive hyperactive behavior.

checks.claim: Cordeddu et al. (2009) delineated the clinical phenotype of patients carrying the same SHOC2 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Review of the clinical features of the SHOC2 mutation-positive individuals revealed a consistent phenotype, previously termed Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the phenotype of the mutation carriers.

checks.claim: Patients carrying the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had a distinctive combination of Noonan-like features and loose anagen hair.
checks.evidence_quote: Overall, these subjects appeared to share a phenotype that was characterized by an unusual combination of features observed in disorders of the neuro-cardio-facial-cutaneous disorders family
checks.explanation: Combined with the Noonan-like facies and loose anagen hair described in the same section.

checks.claim: Patients carrying the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had short stature, frequently associated with proven growth hormone deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: they exhibited reduced growth, which was frequently associated with proven GH deficiency
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients carrying the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Most of them also exhibited darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients carrying the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had a characteristically hypernasal voice.
checks.evidence_quote: The voice was characteristically hypernasal.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Cardiac anomalies were present in most patients carrying the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009).
checks.evidence_quote: Cardiac anomalies were observed in the majority of the cases
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects were significantly overrepresented in patients carrying the SHOC2 mutation compared with the general Noonan syndrome population (Cordeddu et al., 2009).
checks.evidence_quote: with dysplasia of the mitral valve and septal defects significantly overrepresented compared with the general NS population
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients carrying the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had cognitive deficits.
checks.evidence_quote: cognitive deficits, distinctive hyperactive behaviour that improved with age in most subjects
checks.explanation: Cognitive deficits are stated.

checks.claim: Patients carrying the SHOC2 mutation studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009) had distinctive hyperactive behavior.
checks.evidence_quote: cognitive deficits, distinctive hyperactive behaviour that improved with age in most subjects
checks.explanation: Distinctive hyperactive behavior is stated.

paragraphs.text: Cordeddu et al. (2009) showed that the SHOC2 mutation had arisen de novo in the 12 families from which parental DNA was available. In these patients, DNA from several tissues all carried the S2G mutation, which was evidence that the defect had been inherited through the germline.

checks.claim: Cordeddu et al. (2009) showed that the SHOC2 mutation had arisen de novo in the 12 families from which parental DNA was available.
checks.evidence_quote: We observed 21 with the 4A>G missense change and proved that mutations were de novo in twelve families from which parental DNAs were available.
checks.explanation: The 12 families come only from the second cohort (410 subjects). De novo status was also shown in 3 of the 4 first-cohort subjects, so the overall total is 15 families, not just 12.

checks.claim: In patients studied by Cordeddu et al. (2009), DNA from several tissues all carried the SHOC2 S2G mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: For these subjects, DNAs from several tissues were available and all harboured the S2G mutation
checks.explanation: Stated, although the multi-tissue analysis refers to the four subjects in the first cohort.

checks.claim: The presence of the SHOC2 S2G mutation in several tissues was evidence that the defect had been inherited through the germline (Cordeddu et al., 2009).
checks.evidence_quote: all harboured the S2G mutation, providing evidence that the defect was inherited through the germline
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Bertola et al. (2017) described a similar phenotype, PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair (NSLH2), which is caused by mutation in the PPP1CB gene.

checks.claim: Bertola et al. (2017) described PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair (NSLH2), a phenotype similar to NSLH1.
checks.evidence_quote: This report gives further support that this novel RASopathy-PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair-shares great similarity to Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair
checks.explanation: The paper names PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair and says it closely resembles Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair (NSLH1). The NSLH2 and NSLH1 labels are standard naming.

checks.claim: Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair-2 (NSLH2) is caused by mutation in the PPP1CB gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a 12-year-old Brazilian boy with the p.Pro49Arg mutation in PPP1CB, a novel gene associated with RASopathies.
checks.explanation: The abstract links mutation in PPP1CB to this disorder, which it calls PPP1CB-related Noonan syndrome with loose anagen hair.

paragraphs.text: In patients with Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair, Cordeddu et al. (2009) identified a recurrent c.4A-G transition in the SHOC2 gene, resulting in a ser2-to-gly (S2G) substitution. The mutation had arisen de novo in the families from which parental DNA was available. In functional studies, the substitution introduced an N-myristoylation site, which led to aberrant myristoylation of SHOC2. The mutant protein was constitutively targeted to the plasma membrane, and its translocation to the nucleus upon growth factor stimulation was impaired. Expression of SHOC2 S2G in vitro enhanced MAPK activation in a cell type-specific manner.

checks.claim: In patients with Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair, Cordeddu et al. (2009) identified a recurrent c.4A-G transition in the SHOC2 gene, resulting in a ser2-to-gly (S2G) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed an A-to-G transition at position 4 of the gene, predicting the Ser2Gly amino acid substitution (S2G), in four unrelated individuals
checks.explanation: The same change was found again in 21 more subjects, so it is recurrent.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 S2G mutation had arisen de novo in the families from which parental DNA was available (Cordeddu et al., 2009).
checks.evidence_quote: proved that mutations were de novo in twelve families from which parental DNAs were available
checks.explanation: De novo status was also shown in the first cohort.

checks.claim: In functional studies, the SHOC2 S2G substitution introduced an N-myristoylation site, leading to aberrant myristoylation of SHOC2 (Cordeddu et al., 2009).
checks.evidence_quote: shared the 4A>G missense change in SHOC2 (producing an S2G amino acid substitution) that introduces an N-myristoylation site
checks.explanation: The paper also shows [3H]-myristic acid incorporation by the S2G mutant.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 S2G mutant protein was constitutively targeted to the plasma membrane (Cordeddu et al., 2009).
checks.evidence_quote: This acquired fatty acid modification, a unique finding for inherited human disease, results in constitutive membrane targeting
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Translocation of the SHOC2 S2G mutant protein to the nucleus upon growth factor stimulation was impaired (Cordeddu et al., 2009).
checks.evidence_quote: resulting in aberrant targeting of SHOC2 to the plasma membrane and impaired translocation to the nucleus upon growth factor stimulation
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Expression of SHOC2 S2G in vitro enhanced MAPK activation in a cell type-specific manner (Cordeddu et al., 2009).
checks.evidence_quote: Expression of SHOC2(S2G) in vitro enhanced MAPK activation in a cell type-specific fashion.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Komatsuzaki et al. (2010) identified the SHOC2 S2G mutation in patients with a phenotype in the Noonan syndrome spectrum that included loose anagen hair.

checks.claim: Komatsuzaki et al. (2010) identified the SHOC2 S2G mutation in patients with a phenotype in the Noonan syndrome spectrum that included loose anagen hair.
checks.evidence_quote: We found the previously identified p.S2G mutation in eight of our patients.
checks.explanation: In 92 patients with Noonan syndrome and related disorders, the abstract reports the p.S2G mutation in eight. It also says 'easily pluckable/loose anagen hair is distinctive in SHOC2 mutation-positive patients'. Six of the eight had easily pluckable hair and all eight had sparse hair, so the claim matches the abstract.

paragraphs.text: In patients with Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair, Cordeddu et al. (2009) identified a de novo c.4A-G transition in the SHOC2 gene, resulting in a ser2-to-gly (S2G) substitution. The mutation created an N-myristoylation site, which caused aberrant myristoylation of SHOC2 and constitutive targeting of the protein to the plasma membrane. In vitro, the mutation enhanced MAPK activation in a cell type-specific fashion.
